A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work. Their main text, equations, algorithms, Table 1, Figures 1–6, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical definitions, complexity results, proofs, and illustrative constructions. Section 1.1 explicitly describes the work as theoretical; no original empirical results appear in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical results and mathematical examples and adds theoretical discussion. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the reduction constructions in Appendix B are retained. The revised Lemma 5.6 sketch refers more accurately to the modified network already constructed in v1's appendix; it does not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or training/evaluation benchmarks. The same abstract ReLU networks, hyperplane arrangements, SAT constructions, and mathematical examples are considered.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated comparator methods. Additional citations in v2 concern related theoretical research rather than new baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocols appear in either version. The added comments about reduction widths and input dimensions describe existing mathematical constructions, not changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The illustrative constructions and counterexamples in Appendix C are retained. Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or error analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The FPRAS probability guarantee is unchanged; the added explanation of RP concerns theoretical complexity.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 correct counts attached to unchanged region definitions. Figure 1 changes R1 from 3 to 8 and R6 from 8 to 3, with corresponding corrections to intermediate counts. Figure 2 assigns 7, 8, and 9 to R6, R5, and R4 instead of R1, R2, and R3. The illustrated functions are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 6 newly states fixed-parameter tractability in neuron count for Definitions 1–2 and W[1]-hardness in input dimension for Definitions 3–6, the latter citing Froese et al. [2025a]. These extend the stated complexity picture; the existing numbered theorems and appendix proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.1 retain the same contributions: six region definitions, shallow-network counting hardness, deeper-network decision and approximation hardness, and polynomial-space counting for three definitions. The new conclusion restates these claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the ETH lower bound as a curse of dimensionality and adds that relatively few regions need not make counting easy. It also discusses parameter-dependent tractability boundaries and open questions. The original worst-case and practical-efficiency limitations remain.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, encoding information, and detailed network constructions in Appendices A–B are retained. Added asymptotic size commentary summarizes existing reductions; no implementation settings, hardware information, or code/data-access disclosures are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Virmaux and Scaman [2018], Jordan and Dimakis [2020], and Froese et al. [2025a], connecting the work to Lipschitz-constant computation and parameterized complexity. Publication updates to retained references, including Masden, do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 7, expands the computational-complexity primer, reorganizes related-work paragraphs, and makes terminology, header, and bibliographic edits. These are localized changes; the main exposition and appendix proof organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All six figures and Table 1 are retained, with unchanged diagrams. Figure captions 1–2 are corrected, Table 1 entries are reordered, Algorithms 1–2 now share page 10, and Figures 5–6 share page 25. These are limited display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the figure-count inconsistencies with the unchanged definitions and Theorem 3.1, improves the complexity explanations, and adds useful parameterized-complexity context and a conclusion. These improve accuracy and accessibility, while the central results, algorithms, and proof coverage remain substantially unchanged.
